top.para: After two writer agents collided, a register with one open writer, opened at the editor's word with a new key, every commit signed and checked by the validator, and decommissioning that deletes the key; the editor's own signature on registrations is next.

in-short.para: The collision; one writer at a time; opened at my word; signed commits; what the gate refuses; decommissioning; the weakness left.

collision.para: One writer's push was rejected because another had released first, with 1,925 generated files to merge; the rule followed, and with it the newsroom applying its own PKI.

register.para: One file listing every registration with its session, dates, key and approval; six earlier sessions closed without keys; writer-07 is the same session as writer-06 with a new key.

steps.para: The editor's words in a note; open with a new key kept outside the repository; sign each commit over its tree; the validator checks; close by the editor or the next opening; never again.

gate.para: Unsigned, changed after signing, two open, reopened and reused keys are refused; a commit signed by the open registration passes; the first became v0.14.15.

mistake.para: Closing in a test clone deleted the real key, kept in the home directory; it had signed nothing, so the registration was opened again with a fresh key.

weak.para: Approval is a note, not a signature; CI checks only the latest commit; the history was closed by decision; the key dies with the machine.

why.line: Why it matters beyond this newsroom
why.para: Any agent team needs a register, a key per session, signatures over what it does, a gate and dead keys; no platform is required.

limits.para: It does not stop a push, only a release; it covers the writer only; the approval is not yet signed; my interest.

sources.para: My messages of 31 October, the register, tools and check in this repository, and the first signed commit.
